context_prefix_rationale: TSK_STCO_* is consumed by SF_STUCCO_EXT_NC_v1 (41 tasks). Using SCRP_ (StuCco RePaint) eliminates all ID collisions. Verified: TSK_SCRP_* has zero existing usage in id_registry.json. Also verified STRP_* is NOT used (stair riser NC uses STRS_ prefix, stair railing uses STRL_). Pattern follows established convention: SC = stucco, RP = repaint.
scope_summary: Combined condition assessment + prep + prime + finish repaint spec for previously coated exterior stucco and EIFS wall surfaces. Covers assessment (crack assessment FIRST as in NC, EIFS knock test, condition rating per MPI DSD, adhesion test ASTM D3359, chalk rub test, moisture probe, efflorescence scan), surface prep (pressure wash branched by substrate type — 1500-3000 PSI traditional vs <500 PSI EIFS, mildew eradication, efflorescence treatment on traditional stucco, scrape/feather failing areas, crack patching <1/8 inch, surface defect patching with texture match, caulk assessment and replacement per 'Think Like a Water Drop'), state-driven primer (chalk-binding for SS_EXT_CHALKING, alkali-resistant spot prime on exposed bare stucco, acrylic stain-block for general RP adhesion), finish coat application (spray_backroll primary — same as NC, roll fallback, brush detail), interstage inspection/sanding at QT4, final walkthrough, and customer walkthrough (RP-specific occupied home). SF-based with ITM_STUCCO_WALL. QT2-QT4. Flat/satin sheen. 4 SS_EXT_* substrate states. GOOD/FAIR/POOR condition scale. Texture profile remains dominant cost driver (DUAL multiplier). EIFS constraints carry over from NC: elastomeric PROHIBITED on EIFS, LRV >20, <500 PSI wash, insurance verification. Elastomeric available for traditional stucco RP only at QT3/QT4. Lead-safe RRP gate for pre-1978 buildings.

rp_new_tasks.name: Condition Assessment per Elevation
rp_new_tasks.description: RP-specific multi-point assessment: visual inspection, ASTM D3359 adhesion test, chalk rub test, moisture probe at joints/failure areas, substrate state classification. Mandatory before any prep work.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC has no condition assessment — surface is new. RP must classify existing coating condition to drive primer selection and prep intensity.

rp_new_tasks.name: Light Scraping and Feather Sanding (FAIR condition)
rp_new_tasks.description: Scrape loose/failing paint at localized failure areas. Feather-edge sand all scraped areas with 80-100 grit for smooth transition. FAIR condition (SS_EXT_CHALKING or localized SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT).
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC has no scraping tasks — surface is bare. RP condition-driven prep.

rp_new_tasks.name: Heavy Scraping and Feather Sanding (POOR condition)
rp_new_tasks.description: Extensive scrape of peeling/failing paint with carbide scraper. Feather-edge sand all scraped areas. POOR condition (SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT). 2.0x prep modifier.
rp_new_tasks.justification: Heavy scraping for severe deterioration — NC does not have this.

rp_new_tasks.name: Degloss/Scuff Sand Existing Sound Paint
rp_new_tasks.description: Light scuff sand (150-180 grit) or chemical deglosser on sound existing paint (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT) for mechanical adhesion of new coating. Required for GOOD condition surfaces.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC has no existing coating to degloss. RP adhesion preparation.

rp_new_tasks.name: Chalk Remediation Pre-Treatment
rp_new_tasks.description: Chemical chalk remover or additional low-pressure rinse pass on areas with moderate-to-heavy residual chalk after initial wash. SS_EXT_CHALKING surfaces.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC stucco does not chalk. RP-specific chalking remediation before primer.

rp_new_tasks.name: Caulk Joint Assessment per Elevation
rp_new_tasks.description: Inspect all stucco-to-trim joints, expansion joints, and penetration perimeters using 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol. Classify each joint as intact/cracked/failed. Document for caulk removal/replacement scope.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC caulks fresh joints. RP assesses and replaces failed existing caulk.

rp_new_tasks.name: Remove Failed Caulk
rp_new_tasks.description: Cut and remove failed or deteriorated caulk from stucco-to-trim joints. Clean joint faces. Prepare for new caulk application.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC has no caulk removal — joints are new. RP-specific removal before re-caulking.

rp_new_tasks.name: Chalk-Binding Primer - Spray + Back-Roll (Full Surface)
rp_new_tasks.description: Apply chalk-binding primer to full stucco surface via spray+backroll. Required for SS_EXT_CHALKING. Penetrates and binds residual chalk layer to provide adhesion for topcoat.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC does not need chalk-binding primer. RP-specific primer for chalking surfaces.

rp_new_tasks.name: Chalk-Binding Primer - Roll Application (Full Surface)
rp_new_tasks.description: Roll chalk-binding primer on chalking stucco surface. Fallback method for smaller areas.
rp_new_tasks.justification: Roll variant of chalk-binding primer for RP.

rp_new_tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Spot Primer on Exposed Bare Stucco
rp_new_tasks.description: Spot prime exposed bare traditional stucco areas (scraped to bare substrate) with alkali-resistant primer. pH up to 13 requires alkali-resistant primer even on small areas. Brush application on spot areas.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC uses full-field alkali primer. RP uses spot primer only on scraped-to-bare areas.

rp_new_tasks.name: Acrylic Stain-Block Primer - Spray + Back-Roll (Full/Spot)
rp_new_tasks.description: Spray+backroll acrylic stain-block primer for general RP adhesion on SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT/SS_EXT_PEELING surfaces. Provides adhesion bridge between old and new coating systems.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC uses substrate-specific primers. RP needs stain-blocking adhesion primer for previously coated surfaces.

rp_new_tasks.name: Acrylic Stain-Block Primer - Roll Application
rp_new_tasks.description: Roll acrylic stain-block primer. Fallback method.
rp_new_tasks.justification: Roll variant of RP stain-block primer.

rp_new_tasks.name: RP Primer Brush Detail Work
rp_new_tasks.description: Brush primer into detail areas around penetrations, trim transitions, and tight corners. All primer types. RP context.
rp_new_tasks.justification: Re-keyed from NC with RP context prefix.

rp_new_tasks.name: Vehicle/Driveway Overspray Protection
rp_new_tasks.description: RP-specific protection for vehicles and driveways. Occupied home context — vehicles present. Tarp/plastic over vehicles and driveway surfaces within overspray drift zone.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC is unoccupied construction. RP is occupied home with vehicles/driveways to protect.

rp_new_tasks.name: Ground Cover for Scraping Debris
rp_new_tasks.description: Deploy ground-level plastic sheeting below working elevation to contain scraping debris, paint chips, caulk removal waste, and rinse water runoff. Active for FAIR/POOR conditions.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC has no scraping debris. RP prep generates debris requiring containment.

rp_new_tasks.name: Customer Walkthrough
rp_new_tasks.description: Walk project with homeowner. Review completed work. Document any punch-list items. RP-specific — occupied home, customer relationship.
rp_new_tasks.justification: NC is builder relationship. RP is direct homeowner relationship requiring walkthrough.

rp_new_tasks.name: Lead Paint Screening (Shared RRP)
rp_new_tasks.description: XRF or chemical test for lead on existing coating. Pre-1978 buildings. Shared module.
rp_new_tasks.justification: Shared RRP task from MOD_RRP_EXT_CONTAINMENT pattern.

rp_new_tasks.name: RRP Containment Setup (Shared RRP)
rp_new_tasks.description: 6-mil poly ground containment extending 10 ft from structure. Per-elevation setup. EPA RRP Rule compliance.
rp_new_tasks.justification: Shared RRP task.

rp_new_tasks.name: RRP Wet Scraping (Shared RRP)
rp_new_tasks.description: Wet scraping method for lead paint disturbance. Mist surface before scraping to suppress dust. EPA RRP requirement.
rp_new_tasks.justification: Shared RRP task.

rp_new_tasks.name: RRP HEPA Vacuum (Shared RRP)
rp_new_tasks.description: HEPA vacuum all scraped areas, containment poly, and work zone. EPA RRP requirement.
rp_new_tasks.justification: Shared RRP task.

rp_new_tasks.name: RRP Containment Teardown (Shared RRP)
rp_new_tasks.description: Remove containment poly, dispose per EPA requirements, clearance verification.
rp_new_tasks.justification: Shared RRP task.

relevant_findings.topic: Stucco RP carries over ALL NC substrate type constraints unchanged
relevant_findings.finding: The EIFS vs traditional stucco dichotomy is substrate-permanent. All NC constraints transfer directly to RP: elastomeric PROHIBITED on EIFS (catastrophic moisture entrapment), LRV >20 for EIFS colors, <500 PSI wash for EIFS, insurance verification for EIFS, alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare traditional stucco. The substrate type does not change between NC and RP — it is a permanent physical characteristic of the building.

relevant_findings.topic: Texture profile dual multiplier carries over unchanged from NC to RP
relevant_findings.finding: Stucco texture profile (smooth/sand/lace/dash) is a physical surface characteristic that does not change between NC and RP. The DUAL labor+material multiplier transfers directly: smooth=1.00x, sand=1.25x, lace=1.50x, dash=2.00x. Applies to all coating tasks (prime and finish) and material consumption calculations. This remains the dominant cost driver for stucco estimation in both NC and RP contexts.

relevant_findings.topic: Crack assessment remains FIRST prep task in RP — structural hard stop unchanged
relevant_findings.finding: Cracks >1/8 inch on stucco indicate structural movement regardless of whether the surface has been previously coated. Crack assessment is FIRST prep task before any other work. In RP context, cracks may have been previously patched — assess patch integrity and any new cracking through old patches. The HARD STOP rule (>1/8 inch = structural evaluation) is unchanged from NC.

relevant_findings.topic: Four exterior RP substrate states apply to stucco — chalking is common on stucco RP
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior RP uses 4 substrate states: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (adhered, good condition — degloss/scuff only), SS_EXT_CHALKING (UV degradation of binder leaving powdery residue — chalk-binding primer mandatory), SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (cracking, alligatoring — scrape/feather + spot/full prime), SS_EXT_PEELING (active coating lift — heavy scrape + full prime + alkali-resistant spot on bare areas). Chalking is particularly common on traditional stucco due to UV exposure on the textured cementitious surface. EIFS acrylic finish chalks similarly to painted EIFS.

relevant_findings.topic: Condition scale GOOD/FAIR/POOR maps to substrate states and drives prep intensity
relevant_findings.finding: GOOD = SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (1.0x prep). FAIR = SS_EXT_CHALKING or localized SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (1.5x prep). POOR = SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (2.0x prep). Modifiers apply to prep tasks ONLY. Once properly prepared, coating application is identical regardless of original condition.

relevant_findings.topic: RP primer selection is state-driven, not substrate-state-driven as in NC
relevant_findings.finding: NC uses substrate-driven primer: alkali-resistant on all traditional stucco (pH 12-14), acrylic on all EIFS. RP uses coating-condition-driven primer: (1) SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT = may skip prime with verified adhesion; (2) SS_EXT_CHALKING = chalk-binding primer (most common stucco RP primer); (3) SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT/SS_EXT_PEELING = acrylic stain-block full/spot prime PLUS alkali-resistant spot prime on ANY areas scraped to bare stucco (traditional stucco pH 12-14 remains even decades after cure). The alkali-resistant primer requirement is triggered by exposed bare substrate, not by overall condition.

relevant_findings.topic: Caulk assessment and replacement is expanded scope in RP
relevant_findings.finding: NC caulks fresh stucco-to-trim joints. RP assesses ALL existing caulk joints using 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol, removes failed caulk, and re-caulks. Stucco RP caulk scope includes: stucco-to-trim transitions, expansion joints, penetration perimeters (electrical, plumbing, HVAC), window/door perimeters. Failed caulk on stucco is a major moisture intrusion pathway causing coating failure from behind.

relevant_findings.topic: Elastomeric remains available for traditional stucco RP — crack-bridging value increases with age
relevant_findings.finding: Traditional stucco that has developed hairline cracking over time is an excellent candidate for elastomeric coating during RP. The crack-bridging properties (>300% elongation) address the accumulated cosmetic cracking. All NC constraints carry over: PROHIBITED on EIFS, flat sheen only, QT3+ only, 2 coats mandatory, moisture source assessment required. Material cost premium (5-8x acrylic) makes elastomeric a significant upsell that must be justified by actual crack-bridging need.

relevant_findings.topic: Vehicle/driveway protection is RP-specific — occupied home context
relevant_findings.finding: NC stucco is on construction sites without permanent residents. RP stucco is on occupied homes with vehicles, driveways, patios, outdoor furniture, and landscaping in active use. Vehicle/driveway overspray protection zone is RP-specific, particularly critical for spray_backroll method with its 10-15 ft overspray drift.

relevant_findings.topic: RRP lead-safe requirements for pre-1978 stucco buildings
relevant_findings.finding: Traditional stucco buildings from pre-1978 may have original lead-containing coatings. EIFS buildings are post-1980s construction so virtually never have lead paint (but the BUILDING may be pre-1978 if EIFS was retrofit). Pre-1978 flag is project-level. RRP: 2.0x modifier on prep tasks involving paint disturbance, 6-mil poly containment, wet scraping, HEPA vacuum. RRP is uncommon for EIFS but required for compliance when building is pre-1978.
relevant_findings.source: EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745; SF_TRIM_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (RRP pattern)

condition_drivers.impact: Primary configuration dimension. Drives primer selection, prep intensity, and condition scale mapping. SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT = may skip prime. SS_EXT_CHALKING = chalk-binding primer. SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT/SS_EXT_PEELING = acrylic stain-block + alkali-resistant spot on bare areas.
condition_drivers.notes: Per-elevation if conditions differ. Worst-state-wins per v1.

condition_drivers.impact: Simplified 3-tier prep intensity driver. GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x. Prep tasks ONLY — never coating tasks.
condition_drivers.notes: Maps from substrate_state: GOOD=SOUND, FAIR=CHALKING or localized FAILING, POOR=PEELING or widespread FAILING.

condition_drivers.impact: Carries over from NC unchanged. Drives coating system constraint (EIFS = acrylic ONLY), wash pressure (traditional 1500-3000 vs EIFS <500), primer on bare areas (alkali-resistant for traditional), LRV constraint (EIFS only), insurance (EIFS only).
condition_drivers.notes: Permanent physical characteristic of the building.

condition_drivers.impact: DUAL modifier: smooth=1.00x, sand=1.25x, lace=1.50x, dash=2.00x. Affects BOTH labor rate AND material consumption. Carries over from NC unchanged.
condition_drivers.notes: Physical characteristic. Does not change between NC and RP.

condition_drivers.impact: Acrylic is standard for both substrate types. Elastomeric for traditional stucco ONLY (QT3+, flat only, 2 coats mandatory). EIFS = acrylic ONLY. Elastomeric is particularly valuable in RP for crack-bridging aged stucco.
QT2=economy single finish coat. QT3=standard 2 finish coats. QT4=premium with interstage sand and systematic inspection. QT5 excluded (stucco wall field is not fine-finish).
spray_backroll is primary (same as NC). Spray-only PROHIBITED on stucco (backroll mandatory per doctrine). Roll is fallback for small areas. Brush is detail only.
ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Per-elevation attribute. Same as NC.
condition_drivers.notes: Height modifier on all tasks at elevation.

condition_drivers.impact: 2.0x modifier on prep tasks involving paint disturbance. Activates MOD_RRP_EXT_CONTAINMENT. Pre-1978 buildings only.
condition_drivers.notes: Binary gate. Uncommon for EIFS buildings but required for compliance.

quality_differences.description: Economy stucco RP. Light pressure wash (or hose rinse for EIFS). Spot scrape obvious failures only. Chalk-binding primer if chalking. Single acrylic finish coat. No elastomeric option. Minimal inspection. Crack assessment still mandatory.
quality_differences.typical_use: Budget refresh of commercial/rental stucco. No severe deterioration.

quality_differences.description: Standard residential stucco RP. Full pressure wash (appropriate PSI by substrate). Complete scrape/feather of all failing areas. Chalk remediation. State-driven primer. Two finish coats (acrylic or elastomeric on traditional). Clean transitions. Full caulk replacement. Condition assessment with adhesion testing.
quality_differences.typical_use: Standard homeowner stucco repaint. Most common scenario.

quality_differences.description: Premium stucco RP. Full TSP wash. Thorough scrape/feather. Complete chalk remediation. Premium materials. Interstage sand on anomalies (QT4 only). Systematic raking light inspection. Texture-match patch verification. Photo documentation. DFT verification for elastomeric.
quality_differences.typical_use: High-end residential, custom homes, stucco where coating quality is paramount.

notes_for_materials_manager: RP-SPECIFIC PRIMERS needed beyond NC primers: (1) Chalk-binding primer for SS_EXT_CHALKING (most common stucco RP scenario); (2) Acrylic stain-block primer for SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT/SS_EXT_PEELING — provides adhesion bridge between old and new coating systems.

NC alkali-resistant primer (SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ALKALI) still required for SPOT APPLICATION on any areas scraped to bare traditional stucco. Bare stucco remains pH 12-14 even decades after original cure.
NC finish systems (acrylic standard, acrylic premium, elastomeric) transfer directly to RP with same coverage rates and tier assignments.
All NC coating system constraints carry over: EIFS = acrylic ONLY, elastomeric = traditional stucco only at QT3+, oil/alkyd PROHIBITED on both substrate types.
Texture profile dual multiplier on material consumption carries over unchanged from NC.

RP consumables: add scraping tools (carbide scrapers, heat gun), feathering sandpaper (80-100 grit), chalk rub test cloths, chemical chalk remover, adhesion test kit (ASTM D3359 cross-hatch tape), caulk removal tools.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure follows RP pattern: setup -> assess -> prep -> prime -> finish_1 -> interstage -> finish_2 -> cleanup. Plus shared MOD_RRP_EXT_CONTAINMENT.
Crack assessment is STILL FIRST prep task (same as NC) — not a new RP innovation, it carries over.
NEW assessment module for RP: condition assessment, adhesion test, chalk test, moisture probe at joints, caulk assessment per elevation.
Caulk scope expands in RP: caulk ASSESSMENT + caulk REMOVAL of failed joints + caulk APPLICATION of new joints. Three separate tasks vs NC's single caulk apply task.
Scraping tasks branch by condition: light scrape for FAIR, heavy scrape for POOR.
State-driven primer module replaces NC's substrate-driven primer module. Multiple primer types may be used on same project (chalk-binding on field + alkali-resistant spot on bare areas).
Finish coat module structure identical to NC — same spray_backroll/roll/brush variants, same acrylic/elastomeric branching.
Customer walkthrough is RP-specific cleanup task (occupied home, homeowner relationship).
notes_for_estimation_engineer: NC finish coat rates transfer directly to RP — sealed primed surface has similar application characteristics.
Prep task rates are RP-NEW: scraping (50-100 SF/hr by severity), degloss/scuff (200-300 SF/hr), chalk remediation (150-200 SF/hr).
Condition scale modifier: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x — applies to prep tasks ONLY.
RRP modifier: 2.0x on prep tasks involving paint disturbance — stacks with condition scale on prep tasks.
Texture profile dual modifier carries over from NC: smooth=1.00x, sand=1.25x, lace=1.50x, dash=2.00x.
Access modifier carries over from NC: ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50.
QT modifier: QT2=0.85, QT3=1.00, QT4=1.20 — applies to binary coating tasks (same as NC).
Maximum modifier stacking: POOR (2.0x) x RRP (2.0x) x dash (2.0x) x scaffold (1.60) x QT4 (1.20) = 15.36x on worst-case prep task — recommend T&M billing for extreme combinations.
Stacking partition: Prep pool = condition x RRP x access x texture. Coating pool = QT x access x texture x substrate_type. Never cross pools.
RP chalk-binding primer rates: spray_backroll 300 SF/hr, roll 175 SF/hr (slower than NC alkali primer because chalk surface provides inconsistent absorption).
Spot alkali-resistant primer: 40-60 SF/hr (brush on small scraped-to-bare areas).
Caulk rates: assessment 80-100 LF/hr, removal 40-60 LF/hr, application 80-120 LF/hr.

projected_task_count.notes: 52 total tasks across 10 modules (8 owned SCRP + 1 assessment + 1 shared RRP). NC had 41 tasks across 8 modules.
